newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic next-day power soars amid chill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic next-day power soars amid chill.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic soared Wednesday amid very cold weather across much of the country and reduced output from a few regional power stations.
"Everyone came out buying because of the weather," said an East Coast broker.

The price surge appeared not related to higher demand within the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district but in regions west of the PJM where there were talks of transmission problems tied to the deep freeze in much of the Midwest, market sources said.
"Our loads are actually down from yesterday," a PJM trader, adding the mild weather this week has resulted in excess generation capacity in PJM during off-peak periods.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday was quoted at $30.00-$33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up sharply from Tuesday's $24.50-$25.00 Monday's $23.00-$24.50.
A number of next-day deals for firm, peak delivery were heard done in the $29.00-$32.00 area.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Thursday was assessed at $13.00-$14.00, down from Tuesday's $15.00.
Friday's temperatures in the midsection of the eastern seaboard were predicted to range in the 30-50 Fahreheit degrees, down from today's 30-50 degree range.

In the meantime, the 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear generating unit in Pottsdam, Pa., still running at reduced power as the operator tried to correct an "off gas" problem related to air leakage into the condenser.
A 600 MW unit at the coal-fired Homer City, Pa., power station, which was shut Monday due to an oil feed pump problem, was expected to resume operation Thursday.
There were also talks of slightly reduced output at the Keystone coal-fired plant near Johnstown, Pa., this week, according to market sources.
Swing natural gas prices along the East Coast held steady despite another steep drop in NYMEX gas futures. The January Henry Hub contract were 22.0 per million British thermal units midday at $3.950.
Falling in line with gas, January/February 1997 PJM power was pegged at $31.25-$31.40, down from $31.50-$32.00 Tuesday.
March PJM deliveries slipped to $25.00-$25.50, down from Tuesday's $25.50-$25.75.
First-quarter 1997 PJM was quoted at $29.20-$29.50, down from $29.50-$30.00 Tuesday.
Second-quarter PJM remained at $23.15-$23.50.
July/August 1997 PJM power was still assessed near $32.35.
Third-quarter 1997 PJM was pegged at $29.00-$29.25, higher than Tuesday's $28.75-$29.10, and fourth-quarter 1997 PJM remained at $24.00-$24.50.
Calendar 1997 for peak hour delivery in PJM was talked higher at $26.40-$26.70, compared with $26.30-$26.60 Tuesday.
--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622
